articles.title: Equinor Boosts Annual Output Projection
articles.description: A two percent year-on-year growth in production in the third quarter enabled the Norwegian company to capitalize on higher prices for liquids and European gas.

articles.title: Woodside Exits Planned Greater Sunrise Project
articles.description: Timor-Leste's national oil and gas company will take full control of the Greater Sunrise fields in the jointly managed maritime area agreed between the Southeast Asian country and Australia.

articles.title: EQT-Range Deal Will Create $50B Gas 'Champion'
articles.description: The deal will create America's 'leading natural gas company with a pro forma enterprise value over $50 billion', a joint statement outlined.

articles.title: Energy on Edge Ahead of USA Midterms
articles.description: Energy markets remain on edge ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, Macquarie strategists said.

articles.title: Eni Awards Key Contracts for Cronos Gas Project
articles.description: Eni signed the main engineering, procurement, construction and drilling contracts for Cyprus' first natural gas development, designed to supply Europe via Egypt's liquefied natural gas infrastructure.

articles.title: SNOC completes Phase 1 of Hedebah gas-condensate field in UAE
articles.description: SNOC completed Phase 1 development at Hedebah gas-condensate field in Sharjah, resulting in more than a twofold increase in gas production.

articles.title: ANYbotics ships explosion-proof robots for oil and gas inspections
articles.description: ANYbotics has started customer deliveries of ANYmal X, a legged inspection robot certified for use in explosive industrial atmospheres including oil, gas and chemical facilities.

articles.title: Iran Cracks Down on Sinokor Tankers
articles.description: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said it would take 'legal action' against tankers belonging to Sinokor, the world's biggest oil tanker owner that has carried millions of barrels out of the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks.

articles.title: China’s Refiners Turn to Africa and Brazil Crude as Freight Rates Ease
articles.description: China’s refiners are buying crude oil from West Africa and Brazil after freight rates eased in the past two weeks, while competition for Russian supply is stronger and Iranian barrels have disappeared. Following a decline in shipping rates from all-time highs, some Chinese refiners have bought West African and Brazilian crude grades at premiums of up to $20 per barrel above ICE Brent for delivery in December, trading sources told Bloomberg on Wednesday. In early October, the freight rates of crude cargoes from the Atlantic Basin to Asia soared…

articles.title: Iran Eyes $130 Oil While at Least 50 Tankers Sit Stuck in the Gulf
articles.description: An oil price of $130 per barrel could be one of the scenarios of Iran’s economic planners preparing the budget for the next Iranian year starting March 2027, according to Iranian media. It is not clear yet what baseline Iranian economists will use in next year’s budget, but the Plan and Budget Organization may include a scenario assuming $130 a barrel oil, according to Fars News Agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). It is highly unlikely the baseline would be as high as the $130 oil floated…

articles.title: QatarEnergy Extends LNG Force Majeure to End of 2026
articles.description: State-owned firm QatarEnergy has extended the force majeure on LNG deliveries to the end of the year, leaving Europe and Asia without certain term supply heading into the winter, in a move that drove European natural gas prices to the highest level since the autumn of 2022. Italy’s gas importer and energy provider Edison said it had received a notice from QatarEnergy confirming the extension of the force majeure on deliveries – in force since April 2026 – until the end of the year. QatarEnergy has informed Edison that…

articles.title: U.S. Lawmakers Warn Banks Against Trump's Russian Diesel Deal
articles.description: A bipartisan group of US lawmakers has warned American banks, port authorities, and fuel-industry groups against facilitating imports of Russian diesel, raising the prospect of congressional investigations and legal action over President Donald Trump’s decision to ease restrictions on Russian fuel. In letters sent to the chief executives of major US banks and the heads of several port authorities, the lawmakers warned that importing Russian diesel could violate federal law and expose companies to civil and criminal liability. They also said…

articles.title: Bahri Profit Hits $1.36 Billion as the World Scrambles for Tankers
articles.description: Surging tanker rates amid the oil and shipping crisis helped Saudi Arabia’s shipping giant Bahri post a tenfold jump in net profit for the third quarter from a year earlier. Bahri booked a net profit of $1.36 billion (5.1 billion Saudi riyals) for the third quarter, ten times higher than the profit of $137 million (513 million riyals) for the same period in 2025, driven in particular by the Bahri Oil business unit, the Saudi shipping firm said on Wednesday. Compared to the second quarter, Bahri’s profit surged by 85%, the results showed,…

articles.title: US EPA proposes changes to oil and gas emissions regulations
articles.description: The US EPA proposed changes to Clean Air Act oil and gas emissions rules, including provisions for marginal wells and associated gas flaring.

articles.title: Latham & Watkins tops oil and gas M&A legal advisory in Q1-Q3 2026
articles.description: Latham & Watkins is the leading oil and gas M&A legal adviser by both deal value and volume in the first three quarters of 2026 (Q1-Q3).

articles.title: India's Gasoline Demand Could Peak by 2035 as EVs Gain Ground
articles.description: India’s gasoline demand is likely to peak by 2035 amid rising ethanol blending and increased use of vehicles running on batteries and natural gas, according to A S Sahney, the chairman of the largest state-owned refiner, Indian Oil Corporation (IOC). Talking at an industry event in Goa on Wednesday, Sahney said that “Motor spirit is feeling pressure from all sides" as demand for other refined products rises. Diesel and jet fuel demand are set for continued growth amid rising industrial activity and air travel, while demand for fuel…

articles.title: China’s Wind and Solar Power Capacity Surpasses 2 Terawatts
articles.description: China’s total installed wind and solar power generation capacity exceeded 2 billion kW by the end of September, with 170 million kW in new capacity added over the first nine months of the year, the country’s National Energy Administration reported this week. Solar capacity accounted for the bigger portion of that total, at 1.31 billion kW as of end-September, the NEA data showed, while wind capacity hit 700 million kW. For solar, annual growth in capacity stood at 16.5%, while growth in wind capacity stood at 20.4%. “From the…

articles.title: Equinor Profits Triple as Oil and Gas Prices Surge
articles.description: Equinor tripled its adjusted net income for the third quarter from a year earlier, on the back of strong refining margins, high oil and natural gas prices, and increased hydrocarbon production. The Norwegian energy major on Wednesday reported an adjusted net income of $2.86 billion for the third quarter, tripled from the $932 million income for the same period last year. Equinor’s oil and gas production rose by 2% year-over-year to 2.166 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (boepd). Furthermore, the company realized a European…

articles.title: Oil Traders Brace for Iran Escalation After U.S. Elections
articles.description: Oil traders appear to be preparing for a resumption of hostilities in the Middle East following the U.S. midterm elections on November 3, and if such a resumption does not take place, oil prices are likely to drop, ING commodity strategists wrote today in a note. With President Trump repeatedly hinting at or outright saying he may restart attacks on Iran after the midterms, anticipation of new hostilities is only to be expected. However, as ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey wrote, the escalation is not a done deal. And if it does not…

articles.title: Sanctioned Oil Tankers Find a Lucrative New Trade in the Persian Gulf
articles.description: Tankers previously used to ship crude oil from sanctioned countries are now moving crude out of the Middle East, after being removed from sanction lists. Two very large crude carriers that used to transport Venezuelan crude before are now being used to export oil from the Persian Gulf, and two more are en route to the Gulf of Oman, setting off from South America, Bloomberg reported today. “Vessels that were blocked are being delisted or are being licensed for certain forms of financial transactions,” Benjamin Robinson, maritime attorney…

articles.title: Oil Prices Climb as Houthi Attacks Reignite Saudi Supply Fears
articles.description: Oil prices climbed in early Asian trade on Wednesday as renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia reignited supply fears in the region. Falling inventories and reports that the U.S. is preparing for a new military campaign against Iran after the midterm elections added to the upward momentum. At the time of writing, Brent oil futures were trading at $115.70 per barrel, up 1.62% on the session, while West Texas Intermediate futures had risen 1.34% to trade at $101.20 per barrel. The most recent gains came after a nearly $2 decline on Tuesday, a decline…

articles.title: Oil Slips as Iran Diplomacy Picks Up
articles.description: Oil dipped as traders weighed moves to de-escalate tensions in the Persian Gulf and awaited the outcome of consequential elections.

articles.title: America Produces Less Than 1% of the Rare Earth Magnets It Needs
articles.description: China’s ongoing weaponization of rare earths, which has now been bolstered to include measures to keep individuals with sensitive technological knowledge from leaving the country, gives it leverage over a $1.5 trillion U.S. civilian economy that depends on permanent magnets. The Pentagon has spent years preparing for life without Chinese rare earths, but the civilian economy hasn't. IMF researchers identified 34 sectors of the U.S. economy with direct exposure to rare earth supply disruptions, while the International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates…

articles.title: Americans Hit Hardest by War-Driven Oil Price Surge
articles.description: Americans are paying the biggest portion of global energy price inflation resulting from the war in the Middle East, a Finnish energy and climate outlet has reported. Estimating the global total in fuel inflation at $468 billion, the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air said the U.S. portion of this total stood at $160 billion. On a per-capita basis, Americans are also paying the most, CREA also said, estimating their additional costs at $471 per person, while the global total has been estimated at an average of $60.
